newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end lower on fears of oil price rise.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end lower on fears of oil price rise.

text.p: Delhi shares closed sharply lower on Friday after Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral fanned expectations of an increase in the prices of domestic petroleum prices, brokers said.
The Delhi bourse's benchmark index fell 10.56 points, or 1.3 percent, to close at 790.54.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral in an interview on state-run television Doordarshan late on Thursday said his government needed to take a bold decision to contain a high oil pool deficit stemming from subsidised fuel prices.
"Stocks are likely to remain subdued for few more sessions till the finance bill is passed in parliament," said Ravi Batra of brokerage Dewan Securities Pvt Ltd.
Reliance Industries lost four rupees to 304.50.
State Bank of India fell 6.95 rupees to 312.95.
ACC plunged 30 rupees to 1,456 on late selling by traders.
Oriental Bank of Commerce quoted 1.50 rupees down to close at 75.50.
Hindustan Lever Ltd lost five rupees to 1,085.
